children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposits mobilised by banks under the special Reserve Bank of India (RBI) window stood at $132.9 billion according to inflows reported by banks as of September 18, up from the previous update of $127 billion.

Overall inflows amounted to $143.5 billion, inclusive of external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and overseas foreign currency borrowings (OFCBs), according to data released by the RBI on Monday. This is more than five times the $26 billion raised under a similar scheme in 2013. Banks managed to mobilise more money in the last 10 days of the scheme than they did in the first 74 days, when they collected $65.4 billion. "We expect the total inflows to go up to $160 billion by the end of December because the RBI is still providing the hedging facility," said Gaura Sengupta, chief economist at IDFC First Bank.
